t.2.67.1: But having heard that his father was dead and that his two brothers had been sent into exile, Bharata, burning with grief, spoke these words.
t.2.67.2: What use is a kingdom here to me, stricken and grieving, bereft now of my father and of my brother, who was like a father to me?
t.2.67.3: You have heaped sorrow upon my sorrow, as if you had poured caustic salt into a wound, by bringing the king to the state of death and making Rāma an ascetic.
t.2.67.4: You have come like the Night of Doom for the destruction of the family; my father embraced a burning coal and did not realize it.
t.2.67.5: Kausalyā and Sumitrā, tormented by grief for their sons, will hardly be able to go on living now that they have had to deal with you, my mother.
t.2.67.6: Surely the noble one too, righteous of soul and knowing the conduct due to elders, behaves toward you with the most excellent conduct, just as he behaves toward his own mother.
t.2.67.7: Likewise my eldest mother, the far-sighted Kausalyā, abiding by dharma, behaves toward you as toward a sister.
t.2.67.8: Having sent her son, that self-possessed one clad in rags and bark garments, away to dwell in the forest, how is it, O wicked woman, that you do not grieve?
t.2.67.9: Having sent into exile, clad in bark garments, one who sees no evil, a hero, self-disciplined and renowned, what reason do you now see for it?
t.2.67.11: For I, not seeing Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, those tigers among men, by what power and strength could I venture to protect the kingdom?
t.2.67.10: Greedy as you are, I think you did not know how I stand toward Rāghava; that is why you have brought about this great calamity for the sake of the kingdom.
t.2.67.12: For the mighty great king, righteous in soul, always relied upon him, the powerful one, just as Mount Meru rests upon the forest of Meru.
t.2.67.13: How then shall I, like an untrained young steer coming upon the yoke, bear this burden once borne by a mighty draft-ox, and with what strength?
t.2.67.14: Or rather, should I have the power, whether through stratagems or by the strength of my intellect, I will not let you, who are so greedy on behalf of your son, have your desire fulfilled; I will bring back from the forest my brother, beloved of his own people.
t.2.67.15: Having spoken thus, great-souled Bharata, wounding her with torrents of unkind words, and himself stricken with grief, roared once more like a lion dwelling in a mountain cave.
